video.title: How to Use ChatGPT Dots to Build Apps in Minutes (AI + No Code)

summary: Mikey No Code demonstrates a workflow where an AI assistant called 'Dots' (ChatGPT Dots, as titled) researches app ideas and writes three phased build prompts, which are then pasted into the no-code builder Base 44 to build a 'branded carousel maker' web app. The app is built in three phases: manual editor, brand kit/presets/projects, and PDF/PNG export plus JSON backup. The key takeaway is that better upfront decisions (narrow idea, phased prompts with clear limits) matter more than the build speed. The video is also a promotion for the presenter's paid Base 44 master class (offered free via link). No revenue or market validation data is given.

tactics.name: Use an AI planner to pick and scope the idea before building
steps: Ask the AI to research the current app market and propose simple web app ideas with clear problem and real pain demand
Require ideas to be realistic as a proof of concept without a complicated back end
Ask it to explain why each has potential and which is strongest
Choose a small-scope idea with a clear target user and a reason to pay

quote.text: find a few simple web app ideas that solve a clear problem, have real pain demand, and are realistic enough to build as a proof of concept
quote.speaker: Mikey

tactics.name: Phased prompt plan for an AI app builder
steps: Have the planner write three detailed plain-language prompts, one per phase
Each prompt states what to build, what stays unchanged, and what not to add yet
Phase 1: core editor with local storage; Phase 2: brand kit, presets, project library; Phase 3: export and backup/restore
Paste one prompt at a time into the builder and test each phase before moving on

quote.text: Each prompt needs to build on what already exists, of course, rather than say repeating all of the same work over again
quote.speaker: Mikey

tactics.name: Test each phase with a concrete checklist
steps: Create, edit, duplicate, delete slides and reload to confirm autosave
Apply presets, set a brand kit, rename and duplicate projects
Export PDF and PNG, download backup, delete project, re-import to confirm restore

warnings.warning: Vague or overly broad prompts force the AI to make many guesses that stack up; the failure happens before the builder opens.

quote.text: tell it to build an app that does everything, and then well, it has to make dozens of product decisions all on its own, basically guessing
quote.speaker: Mikey

warnings.warning: A good builder cannot fix an idea that is too broad or that nobody would pay for.

quote.text: if the idea is still too complicated or even too broad or something nobody would actually even pay for, well then a good builder isn't going to fix that
quote.speaker: Mikey

warnings.warning: Many people build basic apps that make no money or sites that do not convert (said in a course promotion).

lessons.lesson: With AI builders the bottleneck is decision quality and scope before prompting, not generation speed.

quote.text: a no code builder can move incredibly fast, but it's still only as good as the instruction going into it
quote.speaker: Mikey

lessons.lesson: Ship a narrow proof of concept with a clearly defined user and no backend to cut complexity.
Break builds into phases with explicit exclusions so features do not creep in early and each step can be tested.
Use one AI to plan and another to execute; separating research/planning from building reduces guesswork.

quote.text: Dots just gave us a direction. It broke the idea down into a sensible build order
quote.speaker: Mikey

lessons.lesson: AI-suggested demand is not validation; real willingness to pay still needs testing with actual consultants before investing more.
Client-side-only apps (local storage, in-browser export) avoid hosting and data-protection overhead but limit monetisation (no accounts) until a backend is added.

evidence_quality.rationale: Tutorial demo of an AI-built proof of concept with no revenue, customers or market validation; idea demand is asserted by an AI. Useful as a workflow example only.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sells a Base 44 master class (normally $499, offered free as lead magnet) and promotes Base 44 throughout.
